title: Liu Bai
text: Liu Bai treats blank paper or silk as an active semantic element. Blank regions may represent sky, water, mist, spiritual distance, silence, or atmospheric transition. Sparse compositions should reserve at least one visually continuous blank region.

title: High Distance
text: High Distance depicts the viewer looking upward from the foot of a mountain. The primary peak should occupy the upper or central vertical area, with a compressed foreground and ascending mountain structure.

title: Deep Distance
text: Deep Distance organizes mountains and valleys through overlapping layers that guide the eye from foreground into concealed depth. Mist or water can separate spatial layers.

title: Level Distance
text: Level Distance expands the scene horizontally, often using low mountains, wide water surfaces, distant banks, and extensive blank atmosphere.

title: Host and Guest
text: The dominant motif acts as the host while minor motifs serve as guests. The guest should support rather than compete with the visual hierarchy of the host.

title: Sparse Foreground
text: A sparse foreground may contain one boat, pavilion, scholar, or tree while leaving broad water or mist areas uninterrupted.
